title: Sensitive field sanitizer and backfill coordinator
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: build a schema-aware sensitive-field sanitizer service and a coordinated backfill runner that can scrub or tokenise sensitive values across historical analytics event streams with minimal disruption and provable auditability. This ticket covers the service design, a streaming-safe backfill coordinator, operator tooling, and compliance artifacts for legal/infosec sign-off.

Scope: 1) Sanitizer service that consumes events (both streaming and batch ingestion) and applies scrub/tokenization rules derived from the schema registry; 2) Backfill coordinator that runs incremental re-processing jobs for windows of historical data, tracks progress, and retries with idempotent workers; 3) Shadow audit index containing compact attestations of transformations (hashes + rule IDs) so we can prove actions without storing raw PII; 4) Operator console endpoints for triggering replays, pausing pipelines, and viewing progress; 5) Integrations with KMS for reversible token escrow when legal/business requires reversible mapping under controlled access.

Design notes: - Rules are authored as schema-level annotations in the schema registry (sensitive: {scrub|tokenize|redact|hash}), with an optional rule version. Sanitizer reads rule versions and stores the applied rule id in event metadata. - Streaming path: sanitizer sits as a processing stage on the Kafka topic before materialization to the analytics lake; it must keep per-partition ordering to preserve downstream dedupe semantics. - Backfill path: coordinator schedules windowed backfills using table snapshots and a streaming re-ingest approach to avoid multi-terabyte full-table scans; it keeps a per-window watermark and idempotent marker per event. - Shadow index: a compact column-family store (Bigtable/Cassandra) keyed by original event id -> {applied_rule_id, transformation_hash, timestamp, operator}. The shadow index is the compliance artifact and is queried by audits. No raw PII is stored there. - Escrow keys and reversible tokens are only used when legal requires reversible mapping; access is controlled via role-based access and recorded in audit logs.

Performance targets: - Online sanitizer adds <5ms p50 latency to event ingestion path with peak throughput 20k events/s per cluster. - Backfill coordinator should be able to reprocess 1TB/day per job for typical windows, with horizontal scaling. - Shadow index writes must be capped to <10% of ingestion IOPS to avoid cost explosion.

Success criteria: 1) New sanitizer deployed to dev with e2e test that validates 4 rule types; 2) Backfill coordinator can run a 30-day historical replay on staging and complete within SLA; 3) Compliance team can query shadow index and verify attestations for at least two sample customers; 4) Performance overhead on production ingestion <10% cost increase.

Out of scope: cross-region replication of shadow index (phase 2), GUI-level consent flows (handled by PM), and full DB-level crypto-shredding (separate ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Sanitizer respects schema registry annotations and records applied_rule_id in event metadata for every processed event.
Backfill coordinator exposes windowed watermarks and a public job status endpoint with start/complete/error states.
Shadow audit index contains transformation_hash and applied_rule_id for sampled events and is queryable by the compliance team.
E2E test demonstrates no raw PII remains in analytics sinks for scrub rules and reversible tokens are only stored under escrow with KMS control.
Performance benchmarks: p50 ingestion latency increase <= 5ms, backfill throughput >= 1TB/day on staging cluster configuration.
rollout_plan: Week 0: feature branch + unit tests; design review with Privacy and Platform infra.
Week 1: deploy sanitizer to dev pipeline; run synthetic traffic e2e tests and measure latency.
Week 2: run controlled backfill on staging with a 30-day window; iterate on idempotency and retry logic.
Week 3: security and legal review of shadow index contents + KMS policy; obtain sign-off.
Week 4: canary rollout to 10% production traffic with operator monitoring; run one live backfill on a <7-day window.
Week 5: full production rollout and run a customer-requested replay; produce compliance attestation report.
risks: Unexpected schema churn could require backfills to continuously run; mitigate with rule versioning and incremental delta logic.
Reversible token escrow increases attack surface; require KMS with strict RBAC and recorded access timestamps.
High cost from shadow index at scale; mitigate by sampling and retention policy for attestations.
Backfill jobs can create load spikes on storage; coordinator must coordinate windows to respect capacity budgets.
